CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old patient who presents with right leg pain following a bowling injury. She was running up to the bowling lane while holding her bowling ball, and when she swung it forward, she struck herself in the right leg instead of releasing the ball down the lane. She subsequently fell. She denies significant swelling but reports some bruising on the back of her leg. She has been able to walk only with difficulty and reports significant soreness with ambulation. She would avoid stairs at all costs. She has been managing pain with alternating ibuprofen and Tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema.
Diverticulosis with prior diverticulitis, status post colectomy with partial removal of colon.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide for eczema (uses as needed when itchy).
Ibuprofen (alternating with Tylenol for current pain).
Tylenol (alternating with ibuprofen for current pain).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of right femur: Normal, no evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right leg contusion. Start Mobic 15 mg once daily as anti-inflammatory. Apply ice for pain management. Expected improvement within one week. Patient instructed to return if symptoms do not improve.
